notes: One typescript sheet of corrections and questions referring to pages 11 through 17. It has handwritten pagination - 5 - at the top, archive number 69 at the bottom left, no visible title, and no date. The main text is typed; the appended p.12 reference, the p.13 and p.16 added entries, the two psi glyphs and the final reference numbers are supplied in an unnamed hand. The chi glyphs are mathematically secure but their typed/hand construction remains uncertain, marked at the first occurrence. The author asks for an Exp.V reference; wonders whether the definitions make sense for merely connected C (ending je me canule ?); asks SGA ou EGA ?; notes that the connected-curve fact has already been cited sans référence; asks whether propre et lisse suffices; and objects, with il me semble, that geometric regularity of the fibres need not make an X not assumed flat smooth. Two identities follow, with labels (i) and (ii), and the last sentence ends at ne sont pas. These are author statements, not assertions proved during this reading. No proof or computation was undertaken. H contains description only: it is unavailable as a transcription witness, so every h_reading is null and diff_h is false. The three explicit C doubt marks were all inspected; the two index doubts are retained, while the punctuation doubt after on trouve gains an ellipsis alternative. The unmarked C_context target canule is confirmed with one n. No deletion, independent diagram, title, letterhead, date or marginal note was identified.
math_reading_decisions: First entry: K^{\bullet}(T) and K_{\bullet}(T) have independently visible small solid points above and below the K baseline respectively; neither point is a prime, star or exclamation. Both K and both T are ordinary typed capitals with no independent doubled alphabetic stroke.

All ordinary inline C, S and X capitals were inspected individually: C in the connectedness question and regular-scheme quotation; S in the flatness phrase and henselian quotation; X twice in the non-flatness objection. Their outlines are ordinary typewriter forms, not calligraphic, script or double-struck letters.

The typed Exp.V, EGA IV 2.8 and final V have ordinary unruled Roman letters. The two handwritten p.13 Roman numerals have upper and lower transverse rules and are transcribed separately as overlined/underlined IV and III.
The first and second point indices both lie below their x; the following s is part of each lowered index. Neither alphabetic-versus-numeric doubt is resolved from mathematical expectation.

Both large psi glyphs have a descending central stem and two upward curved arms, unlike a Latin Y or phi; their thin pen construction contrasts with the adjacent typewritten indices. The first subscript is i; the second is i+j, with a crossed plus sign.

Formula (i) was read sign by sign as \psi_i(c^i(x)) = (-1)^{i-1}(i-1)! c^i_{\chi}(x), with upper i on each c, lower chi on the right c, two distinct horizontal equality strokes, negative signs in both relevant places, a genuine factorial exclamation point and its point, the written parentheses, and the final comma. The chi construction is explicitly uncertain in reading.tex.

Formula (ii) was independently read as \psi_{i+j}(c^i(x)c^j(y)) = (-1)^{i+j-1}(i+j-1)!c^i_{\chi}(x)c^j_{\chi}(y), with upper i then j on the product factors on each side, i+j-1 both as exponent and factorial argument, two plus signs in those expressions, and the final comma. Juxtaposition is preserved: no multiplication dots are supplied.

The first c superscript in formula (ii) is the dotted upright i; the next is j with its lower hook. The same i/j distinction is separately visible on the two right-side factors. The variable y has a descending hooked lower part and is not an additional chi.

Each of the three chi signs was cropped separately. The crossing strokes determine the character; their repeated flat head/foot and rougher diagonal leave the construction (typed or manually supplied) uncertain. The recurrence is marked at the first occurrence and the preferred candidate is used thereafter.

The labels (i) and (ii), both formula-ending commas, the absence of any arrow or inequality, and the final reference digits 6.5.3 and 6.6.4 were checked from ink. This is reading of notation only, not a proof check.
